items.title: Robust and Energy-Efficient Controls for a Two-Level System
items.teaser: Robust and Energy-Efficient Controls for a Two-Level System — linked to arXiv:2503.20130.
summary: A two-level Landau-Zener control problem balancing energy cost, transfer fidelity, and robustness against calibration errors.
The energy-minimizing solution is derived with the Pontryagin Maximum Principle and robust controls are optimized with GRAPE.

items.title: Robust Optimal Control for a Two-Level System using GRAPE
items.teaser: 3rd GdR TeQ colloquium and poster session — robust optimal control using GRAPE and research discussions with the community.
summary: Robust and energy-efficient state-transfer controls for an ensemble of two-level systems with Hamiltonian uncertainty.

items.event: Quantum Technologies for Computation and Communication Summer School
items.title: Universally Robust Control for a Qubit under an Unknown Perturbation
items.teaser: Presented “Universally Robust Control for a Qubit under an Unknown Perturbation” at the Quantum Technologies for Computation and Communication summer school at IESC.
summary: Control protocols that retain high fidelity under an unknown static Hamiltonian perturbation for state transfer and gate synthesis.
Robustness is imposed through perturbative cancellation conditions on the Dyson expansion.
